explanation: Advertising executive Martin Speckter proposed it in 1962 for questions asked in excitement or disbelief. Its name joins interrogation with bang, printers' slang for an exclamation mark.

claims.text: The interrobang combines a question mark and an exclamation mark in a single symbol.
The interrobang does not combine a question mark with a full stop, a comma or a colon.
American advertising executive Martin K. Speckter proposed the interrobang in 1962.
The name interrobang joins interrogation (Latin interrogatio) with bang, printers' slang for an exclamation mark.
